dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine, good afternoon.
Hi, yeah, good afternoon. You're on speaker, sorry, my hands are full. My name is Beverly Hazard, I'm calling about 9 Wellington Avenue. The drain on the corner. Again.
Okay, Beverly. 9 Wellington Avenue. Let me pull that up. [pause] Alright, I've got it. I actually spoke with Paulo Raposo on Monday about that address, right?

Yes, Paulo, that's Luis's son. I rent the second-floor apartment there. And I'm calling because honestly, nobody in that house can keep doing this. That basement flooded twice now. Twice this winter. First time was that snow-to-rain storm, the end of January, Sunday night into Monday. Then this weekend, the nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday, same thing all over again. Except worse.
Okay. So I have here the first one reported January twenty-sixth, about three inches of water, and then this past Sunday, the twenty-second, about eight inches. Is that right?

Eight inches, yes. Three, then eight. And you know what happened after the first one? A crew came, the next day, Tuesday. They cleaned the leaves off the top of the grate and they left. That's it. Nothing under the street. And then a month later, here we go.
I do see that note, the crew on January twenty-seventh cleared debris off the grate at the corner.
Right. Off the top. Which, okay, thank you, but obviously that wasn't the problem. Hold on one second. [pause] Spera, spera un bocadinho, N sta na telefoni. [pause] Sorry. Okay. Where was I.
That's alright. You were saying about the grate.

The grate, yeah. So I want to know what's the timeline now. Like, it flooded two times. Two. Is somebody actually fixing the pipe, or are we just gonna wait for the next storm and call you again and do this whole thing again?
I hear you. So where it stands right now, when Paulo called on Monday I logged it as a repeat backup and there's a crew scheduled to go out to that corner today.
Today. Okay. What time today?
It's on today's schedule, so sometime this afternoon. They've got a list after the weekend, so it depends on how the earlier stops go. But it's on there for today, for that corner.
Okay. And are they just gonna sweep the top again? Because I swear—
I can add a note to the work order that the grate was already cleared in January and it flooded again anyway, so they know to look further than the top.

Yes, please put that. Put that in big letters. [inaudible] I'm sorry, it's a little loud here. Seven letters, overflowing... no. Sorry, I'm doing the crossword in the paper while I wait for you guys, it's the only thing keeping me sane today. Okay. Go ahead.
[laughs] No problem. So I'm noting: grate cleared January twenty-seventh, flooded again February twenty-second, eight inches, please check the line beyond the grate. Does that sound right?

That sounds right. And look, it's not even my stuff down there, I don't use the basement, I'm upstairs. But I helped Luis carry everything out after the first time. The paint cans, the ladders, the tools from the workbench, all of it went out to the curb. We already threw that stuff away. Now I come home from work and it's eight inches, and we're out there hauling and mopping again. I'm tired. Everybody's tired of repeating it. Luis is seventy years old, he shouldn't be doing this.
No, I understand. That's a lot, twice in a month.
So I want a supervisor to call me. Not just Paulo, me. Because I want somebody who can actually tell me if there's a real fix coming, not just a crew.

Okay. There's already a supervisor callback set for Paulo by tomorrow, Thursday. But I can put in a separate one for you, too. And I'm also going to flag the history on this for engineering, since it's the second time, so they can look at whether something bigger needs to happen at that corner.
Okay. Good. Engineering. That's what I wanted to hear, honestly. Because two times, and the next one, what, it's gonna be a foot?
I'm putting it in now. What's the best number for the supervisor to reach you?
401-555-0161. And that's Beverly, B-E-V-E-R-L-Y, and last name Hazard, like H-A-Z-A-R-D?
Yes. Like the road sign.
Got it. And you said you're the tenant on the second floor at 9 Wellington.
Second floor, yes. [crosstalk] Sorry, what? Did you say something?
I just said I've got that down. Tenant, second floor.
Okay. I'm at work during the day, I'm a school secretary, so if they call and I don't pick up, tell them to leave a message, please. Don't just hang up and mark it done.
I'll put that right in the note. Leave a voicemail if no answer.
Thank you. Because that's what I'm worried happens. Somebody checks a box and then it rains and here we are again.

So just to read it all back. Crew going out to the corner this afternoon, note on it to check below the grate. History flagged for engineering. And a supervisor callback for you at 401-555-0161, voicemail is fine.
Okay. Yeah. That's everything. And if the crew finds something today, can somebody tell Luis? He's home all day.
I'll add that too, that the owner's home and would like to hear what they find.
Okay. Thank you, Lorraine. I'm sorry I'm being short with you, it's not you. It's just, twice.
You're fine. I'd feel the same way. Hopefully the crew gets some answers this afternoon.
Hopefully. Alright. Bye.
